clue.text: Refund arranged by motorway business somewhere in east Scotland

indicators.note: letters that are arranged are put into a new order, so the word refund is reshuffled

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1
a line is a line of business, a trade or occupation

explanation.surface: Someone trades a refund for a road-haulage contract somewhere north of the border.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunfermline is a town in Fife, on the east side of Scotland, so it is one example of such a place.

clue.text: Road runs through disreputable place

indicators.note: one thing running through another sits inside it, so the runs letter goes into the seedy venue

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar or club
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A street cuts straight past a seedy bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive is a road, often a residential street or a private approach to a house.

clue.text: Cathedral reflected on woody plant around embankment

indicators.note: a reflection shows a word mirror-wise, so the little word on is read backwards
the plant's letters go around the bank, holding it inside

parts.note: a tree is a woody plant
a dam is an embankment built to hold back water

explanation.surface: A cathedral's image is mirrored beside a tree growing round a river bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Notre-Dame is the famous Gothic cathedral in Paris, so it is an example of a cathedral.

clue.text: Secretly listen in on insect

definitions.meaning: to eavesdrop, as a verb, a British informal usage
the small pincered creature once thought to crawl into sleepers' ears

explanation.surface: Someone eavesdrops on a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: The insect's name doubles as a British verb for eavesdropping, from the idea of creeping into the ear.

clue.text: Doctor constrains old disorderly crowd

indicators.note: to constrain is to hold in, so the doctor letters hold the old letter inside them

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor holds back an elderly, rowdy crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A mob is an unruly, disorderly throng of people.

clue.text: Popular religious fraternity operating appropriately

parts.note: something in is fashionable or popular
an order is a religious community, such as the Benedictines

explanation.surface: A well-liked brotherhood of monks runs things properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is in order is working correctly or permitted, functioning as it should.

clue.text: Stoats reportedly deal with major English road

parts.note: a stoat in its white winter coat is called an ermine

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the phrase about stoats is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: to treat something is to deal with it

explanation.surface: Stoats seem to be handling a busy route across England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' covers the whole phrase: ERMINES TREAT, said aloud, is the road's name, with the S of ERMINES heard at the start of the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermine Street was the great Roman road running from London north to Lincoln and York.

clue.text: Remote observatory room with office

parts.note: room in the sense of space, as in room to move
a station is a post or position, an office held

explanation.surface: An isolated stargazing building comes with a room and an office.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbiting space station is a crewed outpost far above Earth from which observations are made.

clue.text: Munch, say, French bread with endless seabird

parts.note: pain is the French word for bread

indicators.note: without its end, so the seabird loses its final letter

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Someone chews French bread alongside a seabird with its tail cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Munch' looks like eating; it is Edvard Munch, the Norwegian artist of The Scream.
explanation.definitionFit: Edvard Munch was an artist, so he is an example of one who works in paint.

clue.text: Brush sleeping area when Ed leaves

indicators.note: when Ed leaves, his name's letters go out of the room word

parts.note: a bedroom is where one sleeps

explanation.surface: Ed walks out, and the bedroom gets swept.
explanation.definitionFit: A broom is a long-handled sweeping brush.

clue.text: Rather smart bar is in outskirts of Christchurch

indicators.note: the bar and is go in between the outskirts
outskirts are the edges, so only the first and last letters of the city name are used

parts.note: a lever is a bar used to prise
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rather stylish bar sits on the edge of a New Zealand city.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -ish softens clever to mean somewhat bright, a moderate degree of intelligence.

clue.text: Top act, male, extremely assured on ship

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: the extremes are the outer letters, the first and last of assured

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A star male performer, supremely confident, plays aboard a cruise ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A headliner is the main performer on a bill, the star turn advertised at the top.

clue.text: Daughter favoured loud noise

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees
in, as in in favour, popular

explanation.surface: A favourite daughter makes a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: A din is a loud, confused, prolonged noise.

clue.text: Second American drinking tea, for example

indicators.note: a drinker takes the tea in, so the American letters hold it

parts.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A second American sips tea, to name one instance.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces examples, meaning like or including, the same job as the definition.

clue.text: Indian side-dish bloke consumed shortly before one

parts.note: chap and bloke are both informal words for a man

indicators.note: cut short, so consumed loses its final letter

parts.note: ate means consumed, eaten
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man wolfs down an Indian side dish just before one o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is an unleavened flatbread served alongside curry in Indian cooking.

clue.text: Constellation Greek character starts to recognise using specs

parts.note: tau is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: the starts of the next three words, their first letters

explanation.surface: A Greek man needs his glasses to identify a star pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Taurus, the Bull, is a constellation of the zodiac.

clue.text: Ring tax company about book of a certain size

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: Phone the tax firm about a book of a particular format.
explanation.definitionFit: Octavo is a book format in which each printed sheet is folded to make eight leaves, giving a certain size.

clue.text: Turkish leader Afghan regularly avoided

indicators.note: letters avoided at regular intervals, so every other one is dropped and the rest kept

explanation.surface: A Turkish commander keeps steering clear of an Afghan.
explanation.definitionFit: An aga was a title for a military commander or chief official in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Sword European unknown primarily carried before burial at sea

parts.note: X is the algebraic unknown

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of carried
at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of burial are scrambled

explanation.surface: A legendary sword is borne by a foreigner before a funeral at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' looks like the setting of the burial; it scrambles BURIAL into ALIBUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Excalibur is the sword of King Arthur in British legend.

clue.text: British fighting force is nuts

parts.note: an army is a fighting force

explanation.surface: Britain's armed forces are crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Barmy is British slang for crazy, the same as nuts.

clue.text: Visual representation that is covering magazine

indicators.note: the letters for that is cover the magazine, wrapping round it

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A picture is the thing on the front of a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or likeness, a visual representation of something.

clue.text: Old English letter seen in archive throughout

indicators.note: the letters can be seen inside the words archive throughout, across the gap

explanation.surface: An Anglo-Saxon character turns up all through the archive.
explanation.definitionFit: Eth was a letter in Old English script, written like a crossed d and standing for a th sound.

clue.text: Horseracing venue isn't gratis, except for female

parts.note: ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

indicators.note: except for means leaving out, so the letter for female is dropped

parts.note: gratis means free of charge

explanation.surface: A racecourse charges admission, unless you are a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree, near Liverpool, is the racecourse that hosts the Grand National steeplechase.

clue.text: Amiable sound of horse, big and sturdy, circling ring

parts.note: a neigh is the cry a horse makes

indicators.note: the big word circles round the ring letter, holding it inside

parts.note: burly means big and strongly built
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A horse whinnies as a big, strong one goes round the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound of horse' looks like a homophone signal; it simply means NEIGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Neighbourly means friendly and helpful, in the manner of a good neighbour, so it fits amiable.
